input.question: What is the evolutionary purpose of having different blood types (A,B,AB,O)?
input.ground_truth: While this doesn't answer your question, it is important to understand that evolution does not have a purpose. Mutations do not happen because they can be beneficial. Random mutations happen in individuals, then over time if the mutation is beneficial and propagated via offspring, the lineage with that trait may be more fit than individuals without that trait and slowly become more predominant. A more accurate question would be "Why did organisms evolve different blood types?" I'm not trying to be pedantic for the sake of pedantry, but I think maybe this will help you understand other's answers a little more clearly.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What is the evolutionary purpose of having different blood types (A,B,AB,O)?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your blood is like a team of little helpers that travel around your body to give you energy and help you stay healthy. Now, everyone’s team of helpers has a special name tag—like a badge. Some people have a badge that says “A,” some say “B,” some say “AB,” and some say “O.”

A long, long time ago, people lived in different places and sometimes got sick from different germs. The different badge names (blood types) helped people’s bodies fight those germs in different ways. If one kind of helper (blood type) was good at fighting one kind of germ, and another was good at fighting a different germ, then when people had babies, the babies could get a mix of helpers. This way, the team of helpers could protect people from lots of different germs.

So, having different blood types is like having different superheroes in your body, ready to help you stay healthy in many ways!
